candidate.cwe: CWE-22 path traversal / arbitrary local file read with exfiltration through a confused-deputy upload (CWE-441)

entry_point: MCP tools (issue create/update attachments & description, wiki create/update page body and comment body from a file path) and the equivalent JiraFetcher/ConfluenceFetcher public API

verified.exploit_entry_point: Two real surfaces, Atlassian client always a MagicMock so no network: (a) the fetcher public API (JiraFetcher/ConfluenceFetcher attachment helpers and JiraFetcher.create_issue), which is where the file bytes are read and handed to Atlassian; (b) the MCP tools (create_page/update_page/add_comment/create_issue/update_issue) driven through an in-memory FastMCP Client, exactly as the project's own server tests do.
variants: Jira attachment upload: absolute path outside the workspace, relative ../ traversal, in-workspace symlink to outside, one bad path in a list, the same list under update_issue, the same list spelled as a JSON-array string, the same list spelled comma-separated, and the path list tucked inside the call's fields JSON and inside its additional_fields JSON (src/mcp_atlassian/jira/attachments.py:353-415, update_issue attachments at src/mcp_atlassian/jira/issues.py:1229-1233)
Confluence attachment upload: absolute outside, relative ../, symlink escape, one bad path in a list (src/mcp_atlassian/confluence/attachments.py:124-197)
Page body from a caller-supplied file path on create_page and update_page: absolute outside, relative ../, and a home-expanded path (src/mcp_atlassian/servers/confluence.py:117-153)
create_issue attachments (injected sibling S1): absolute outside, relative ../, symlink escape (src/mcp_atlassian/jira/issues.py:647, 777-791)
create_issue description from a caller-supplied file path (injected sibling S2) (src/mcp_atlassian/servers/jira.py:172-209)
add_comment body from a caller-supplied file path (injected sibling S3): absolute outside and relative ../ (src/mcp_atlassian/servers/confluence.py:1237-1283)

verified.project_tests_run: tests/unit/jira/test_attachments.py, tests/unit/confluence/test_attachments.py, tests/unit/servers/test_confluence_server.py, tests/unit/servers/test_jira_server.py — 293 pass on pinned+injected and on oracle (16 cases that encode the pre-fix unconfined upload/content-file behaviour the published fix reworked are deselected in test.sh; a correct fix changes that behaviour). wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the refusal contract accepts any client error and the upload helpers already catch exceptions and return a failure dict; a crash on a legitimate in-bounds operation is caught by the functional suite.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: each operation confines the exact path it is about to read; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource to authorise instead of the file touched.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: a filesystem confinement has no peer or direction dimension; the attachment-upload and body-from-file routes are enforced by separate tests, not a single toggle.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the protected sink is reading an out-of-workspace file and sending it onward; every route is a read-then-send, so there is no separate write-only guard to get wrong.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the confinement resolves symlinks and '..' itself, so there is no earlier lossy normalisation step a fix would place its check after and silently defeat; the home-expansion shape covers the one ordering hazard (expand before confining) the family has.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the input is a filesystem path, not a parsed identity whose malformed spelling could make the guard see nothing.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: confinement is purely path-based; there is no external authority that could return nothing and make the guard fail open.
